name: Paraswap Augustus V6 uniswapV3SwapCallback missing caller check
race_type_reason: Yoink's tx is the first direct call to Augustus V6's uniswapV3SwapCallback entry in the scanned range; no earlier or same-block attacker tx exists, and the next such call is 11 h 13 min later by independent actors who did not replay Yoink's calldata.
one_liner: Yoink was the first to exploit Paraswap Augustus V6's missing callback caller check, pulling 12,479 OPSEC (6.46 WETH) from one approving wallet 11 hours before anyone else; no return to the victim or Paraswap found.

loot.gross_loot_method: WETH.withdraw ETH delivered to the Yoink contract in the bot tx trace, from selling 12,479.437 OPSEC (pulled from victim wallet 0x0cc396f5 by Augustus V6) into Uniswap V3 pool 0x45f4d604

captured_native.desc: OPSEC transferFrom the approving wallet 0x0cc396f5 to the V3 pool, sold for 6.4633 WETH

loot.loot_note: Scope is tx0 (index 0): gross 6.4633 ETH, 99.8% (6.4504) paid to the coinbase, priority fee 0. The builder refund (index 13, 4.3369 ETH) is a block-level remainder: coinbase payments in the block are 6.5484 ETH (tx0 + tx1), proposer got 2.2229 ETH, so the refund also covers Yoink's arbitrage tx1 (net +0.0092 ETH). bot_net = gross - coinbase + refund; with tx1 included the incident's figure is 4.359 ETH.

fate.returned_desc: No return to the victim wallet 0x0cc396f5 or to Paraswap/Velora found. Checked: no Yoink -> victim transfer in blocks 19470561-19475000 (trace_filter, empty) and the victim's inbound ETH to block 19490000 is only two transfers from 0x3fc91a3a (5.905 ETH total, blocks 19470763 and 19471472, source unknown and not shown to be a Yoink or Paraswap return). Full-history check of Yoink's later flows was not done. 'None found' is not 'none'.
fate.public_statement: Velora post-mortem (not retrievable here, HTTP 403) reportedly lists ~$24K initial loss matching this tx; DeFiHackLabs and Etherscan label the actor a whitehat, which on-chain behaviour does not support.
fate.return_status_rule: returned = everything went back to the victim side except a bounty the victim agreed to or offered; partial = some came back, otherwise; none = known zero within the documented search window; unknown = unresolved

evidence_notes: site/raw/rpc/trace_0x35a73969f582872c25c96c48d8bb31c23eab8a49c19282c67509b96186734e60.json: tx0 = Yoink contract -> Augustus V6 0x00000000fdac... selector 0xfa461e33 (callback entry) at depth 1 with no Augustus swap above it; Augustus then calls V3 pool 0x45f4d604 swap(recipient = Yoink) and pulls OPSEC from the victim wallet via transferFrom; WETH.withdraw then coinbase transfer.

Across the 253 saved trace_filter chunks (blocks 19426044-19481999, toAddress = Augustus) the earliest call to 0xfa461e33 at trace depth <= 1 is this tx (19470561/0); the next is block 19473885 (11 h 13 min later), then 19474732.

incidents/paraswap-2024/callback_calldata_words.json: same selector and layout in the later actors' calls but different victim/token/amount, so they are independent uses of the bug, not replays of Yoink's calldata.
Bribe rule: msg.value 998 (per mille) x 6.4633 WETH = 6.4504 ETH, equal to the coinbase transfer in the trace; builder 'I can haz block?' then refunded 4.3369 ETH at index 13.
